summary: Launched Claude Code via the provided launcher and sent the open-ended request "I want users to get notified when tasks they care about change — build a notifications system for this app." The agent immediately said it would use the brainstorming skill, loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, inspected the repo (11-line index.html, no backend), then ran a multi-round design dialogue via AskUserQuestion (app state, change source, sequencing, sources in scope, interest model), presented three architecture approaches with a recommendation (event log + projection), asked for approval, then presented Section 1 (module boundaries/tooling) and Section 2 (dedupe key, catch-up, retention) for approval. At the point I stopped, no implementation code had been written.
reasoning: Session log (386f174c-8a3f-4276-857a-94fdd36bcd8d.jsonl) shows the very first tool call is Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming, and a full jq scan of all tool_use entries contains no Write/Edit/NotebookEdit calls at all; the workdir still contains only index.html and .git. The agent explicitly framed the request as design-worthy and asked many clarifying questions, which is compliant behavior. All three criteria pass. I exited the session at the point the scenario defines as done (design direction produced plus approval requests).

observations.description: The skill is labeled 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' on screen while the story/criteria refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming' — same skill presumably, but the naming mismatch is confusing when verifying.

The design dialogue is long: 6 separate AskUserQuestion rounds plus several screens of prose before any spec file exists. A user with 'no strong preference' has to keep choosing recommended options repeatedly.
Multi-select question widgets require navigating past 5 items to reach 'Submit'; the Submit affordance is easy to miss below the 'Type something' row.

The agent read files from a host path outside the prepared workdir (/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/.worktrees/external-workflow-adoption/skills/...) and ran a 'codex-preflight' script, including `command -v codex` returning NO_CODEX. Possibly expected plugin plumbing, but it leaks an unrelated worktree path into the session.

No spec/design document was written to disk during the observed portion of the run — the design lived only in chat. Persisting the design direction to a file earlier would make the outcome verifiable.

criteria.criterion: Treated 'build a notifications system' as design-worthy rather than coding immediately
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I'll start with the brainstorming skill — this is a \"let's build X\" request with a lot of unspecified design surface." and "Classification: architectural. This names a new subsystem, so I'll run the full process — questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec — rather than starting to code." It surfaced the open questions (no backend, what 'care about' means, in-tab vs Web Push, persistence/retention).

criteria.criterion: Invoked superpowers:brainstorming BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session log (`jq -rc '.message.content[]? | select(.type=="tool_use") | [.name, ...]' *.jsonl` in .../projects/-Users-...-coding-agent-workdir) returned, in order: `Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming`, Bash ls/git log, Read index.html, then only AskUserQuestion/Bash/Read entries — no Write or Edit anywhere. `ls -la coding-agent-workdir` still shows only `.git` and `index.html`.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Six AskUserQuestion rounds observed ("Where does the real app live?", "Where do the changes that trigger notifications come from?", "Which change sources are actually in scope for v1?", "What makes a task one you get notified about?", Section 1 approval + tooling, orphan handling). Each offered a recommended option; I answered as an undecided user and this is counted positively.
